verdict: Visa's net revenue rose 15% to $10.9B as payments volume grew 8% and cross-border volume 12% — profit rose 14% to $5.9B despite a $707M litigation provision, helped by a one-off $333M tax benefit.

segments.name: Service revenue
segments.note: Fees from banks for using the Visa brand and network on cards — based on the prior quarter's payments volume.

segments.name: Data processing revenue
segments.note: Fees for clearing and processing each transaction — processed transactions grew 9%.

segments.name: International transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees when a card is used outside its home country — cross-border volume rose 12% in constant dollars.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Value-added services — fraud tools, data and consulting for banks and merchants.

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Pay and benefits for Visa's workforce.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

opex.name: Litigation provision
opex.note: Almost entirely the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL) case — a legal charge Visa excludes from its non-GAAP results.

opex.name: Network, professional & depreciation
opex.note: Network and processing ($233M), professional fees ($208M) and depreciation & amortization ($326M).

follow100Note: Per $100 of gross revenue (before client incentives). Measured against Visa's reported net revenue of $10.9B instead, the kept profit is $53.69 per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Volume growth stayed strong
takeaways.text: Net revenue rose 15% to $10.9B — data processing +17%, service revenue +13%, other revenue +33% and international transactions +6%. Payments volume grew 8% in constant dollars, cross-border volume 12% and processed transactions 9%.

takeaways.title: EPS rose 17%
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS rose 17% to $3.03 and net income 14% to $5.9B. Non-GAAP EPS, which strips out the litigation charge and other one-offs, was $3.17, up 15%.

takeaways.title: The legal bill spiked again
takeaways.text: The litigation provision included a $707M special item for the interchange MDL case — in November, Visa signed a superseding settlement agreement for the injunctive-relief class claims, still subject to court approval. A one-off $333M deferred tax benefit, from a change in U.S. taxation of certain foreign earnings, pulled the GAAP tax rate down to 13.0%.

oneTimers: A litigation provision of $707M (the special item within the $708M provision line) for the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL) case sits in operating expenses; Visa excludes it from non-GAAP results.

Also excluded from non-GAAP results: $66M of amortization of acquired intangible assets and acquisition-related costs, and $7M of net losses on equity investments. GAAP results also include a $333M deferred tax benefit from a change in the U.S. taxation of certain foreign earnings. Non-GAAP net income was $6.1B ($3.17 per share).
otherDetail: Investment income and other gains of $183M, less $194M of interest expense — net -$11M.
footerNote: Visa reports 'net revenue' of $10,901M; this page starts from gross revenue of $15,170M so the $4,269M of client incentives shows as a cost.
